name: INTERNATIONAL MONEY EXPRESS INC

priced.reason: book method needs rotce_override or final_growth

devils_advocate.strongest_counter: That the market is undervaluing the litigation badly. Western Union terminated AFTER the last regulator approved and then withdrew its own application to that regulator - conduct that is at least arguable evidence it no longer wanted the deal rather than that it was prevented from closing. The 2026-09-24 pass already recorded that Western Union's $27.3M break fee was conditioned on ANTITRUST failure and so would not be triggered by a licensing failure; the mirror of that is that an unprotected walk-away is also an unprotected BREACH if the condition was in fact satisfied. Intermex has said in a filed document that it remains ready to close and is reserving specific performance. If that claim is worth even a quarter of the $9.61 per share spread, the stock is materially mispriced.
devils_advocate.what_would_prove_it: A complaint filed in Delaware and the court's treatment of the reasonable-best-efforts claim; any settlement; or Western Union's own disclosure of its reserve against the claim.
devils_advocate.already_visible: Only the pleadings-by-press-release so far: Intermex's 8-K sets out its position, and press coverage confirms both sides are preparing for court. Nothing has been adjudicated.
devils_advocate.unresolved: The entire payoff. I cannot handicap a Delaware specific-performance claim, and I should not pretend to. I also note the 2026-09-24 pass estimated a $5-8 break price and the stock has settled at $6.39, so the standalone valuation it reached appears to have been about right - but that is calibration on the easy half of the question.

what_changed: Everything the 2026-09-24 pass nominated as its test arrived, and in an order nobody would have forecast. On the evening of 2026-11-10 - the outside date - the California DFPI, the sole remaining regulatory approval, APPROVED the merger subject to conditions. Shortly after receiving that approval Western Union delivered a notice purporting to terminate the merger agreement on the outside-date right. Intermex responded the same night, refused the termination, stated that all conditions had been satisfied or that their failure was caused by Western Union's breach of its reasonable-best-efforts obligations, demanded that Western Union rescind and close, and reserved the right to seek specific performance and damages for wrongful termination. On 2026-11-11 Western Union notified the DFPI of its purported termination and WITHDREW its application. The 8-K carrying this is dated 2026-11-12 under item 1.02. Separately, the Q3 10-Q of 2026-11-09 shows the standalone decline above, and cash flow flattered by a $48.0M release of prepaid wires (from $59.5M to $11.4M) - nine-month operating cash flow of $83.5M against $52.5M is mostly that working-capital liquidation, not earnings.
consensus_case: At $6.39 against a $16.00 cash deal price, the market has written the Western Union merger off almost entirely and is pricing Intermex as a standalone, shrinking remittance processor. That is defensible: Q3 revenue fell 18.4% to $126.4M and nine-month revenue 17.6% to $379.5M, nine-month operating income fell 51% to $21.5M and net income 62% to $9.0M, and the decline is structural - immigration enforcement is shrinking the sending population in the Latin America corridors while Remitly and other digital competitors take share from an agent network. On 30.2M shares the equity is $193M against $211.2M of cash and $171.4M of drawn revolver, so the market is paying roughly 4-5x EBITDA for a business losing a fifth of its revenue a year, with buybacks frozen since June 2025 by merger covenants. The litigation claim against Western Union is being valued at close to nothing, which is what the market usually does with contested contract claims.
base_case_rationale: No cash-flow base case is appropriate and no book-value base case is admissible. The engine prices this as a financial on justified price-to-tangible-book, and that is a category error which the engine's own flag identifies correctly: Intermex is an agent-network remittance processor whose productive asset is a distribution network and whose $2.70 of tangible book per share is a working-capital balance, not regulatory capital constraining how much business it can write. Supplying a sustainable ROTCE would launder that category error into a fair value. Beyond the method, the price now contains a contested legal claim - specific performance or damages against Western Union for terminating minutes after the last regulator approved - whose expected value turns on a Delaware contract question about reasonable-best-efforts obligations that I cannot adjudicate and will not guess at.
key_risks: Standalone revenue declining 18% a year with no stabilisation visible; nine-month operating income down 51%
Nine-month operating cash flow of $83.5M is flattered by a $48.0M prepaid-wires release - a shrinking business liquidating float, not earning power
$171.4M of drawn revolver against a falling EBITDA base; buybacks suspended since June 2025 under merger covenants, with $48.3M of authorisation unused
The litigation outcome is binary and unhandicappable, and litigation expense is itself a drag
watch_for: A complaint filed against Western Union and any ruling on specific performance or on the reasonable-best-efforts claim
Whether the board restarts the $48.3M of remaining buyback authorisation now the merger covenants have lapsed
Q4 revenue: a fourth consecutive quarter near -18% sets the standalone value lower than the current price implies
